ai.description: The Yembung Sucker Frog (Ranidae) reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with dark mottling and a distinct white upper lip. It features large, adhesive toe discs and a prominent ventral sucker for fast-flowing water.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops gerbillus* is best distinguished from similar species by the presence of a distinct, white, glandular supratympanic fold that lacks a dark border.
ai.habitat: *Amolops gerbillus* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical evergreen forests at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters in the Eastern Himalayas.
ai.behavior: The Yembung Sucker Frog is primarily nocturnal, utilizing specialized adhesive discs on its digits to cling to slippery, vertical rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops gerbillus* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch size data remains undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Yembung Sucker Frog is endemic to Northeast India, specifically found in the state of Arunachal Pradesh at elevations ranging from 400 to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Amolops gerbillus* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps emitted by males perched on rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
